title: SecOps-NG Per-Rule-Version Effectiveness Snapshot (F-WF-04 SKELETON stub)
description: Per-rule-version effectiveness-metric snapshot stub emitted by the F-WF-04 detection-engineering rule lifecycle's `measure` state. One snapshot is produced per (rule_id, rule_version) per evaluation window and pins, mechanically, the value an effectiveness indicator took for that exact rule version, with pointers to the OCSF source-data shape the indicator was derived from and a reference-visualisation hint the downstream F-CP-06 effectiveness evidence stream can consume. SKELETON: this stub commits to the field shape; CORE-FANOUT tightens the value constraints (closed enums, regex patterns) and adds the per-target reference emitters. Public-bar artifact: all string fields stay role-shaped; individual personal names, credential-shaped strings, and raw measurement payloads carrying personal data are out of scope per AGENTS.md §3 and rejected at the schema boundary by the hygiene linter.

schema_version.description: Pinned schema version. Lets a consumer reject snapshots produced under an older schema once breaking changes ship.

snapshot_id.description: Stable per-snapshot identifier. SKELETON: any non-empty string is accepted. CORE-FANOUT pins this to a SHA-256 hex digest derived deterministically from `<rule_id>|<rule_version>|<captured_at>|<metric.stable_id>`.

rule_id.description: Stable identifier of the detection rule the snapshot describes. Opaque to the framework; the operator's detection store assigns it.

rule_version.description: Version label of the detection rule this snapshot pins its measurement to. One rule version produces one snapshot per evaluation window per metric.

captured_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp at which the indicator value was evaluated. Mechanical wall-clock from the workflow runtime; not a measurement-window boundary.

metric.description: The effectiveness indicator the snapshot is reporting one value of, structurally referenced rather than duplicated. Joins back into the metric catalogue at `content/metrics/<stable_id>.yaml` so the catalogue entry's `unit`, `direction`, `thresholds`, and `formula` stay canonical.

stable_id.description: Stable id of the metric in the catalogue (e.g. `kpi.detection_coverage@v1`, `kpi.false_positive_rate@v1`).

definition.description: One-sentence operator-facing definition of what the indicator measures for this rule version. Prose mirror of the catalogue entry's `summary`; carried inline so a consumer reading a single snapshot does not need to dereference the catalogue.

unit.description: Measurement unit. SKELETON accepts any non-empty string; CORE-FANOUT pins this to the catalogue enum (`ratio`, `count`, `duration_seconds`, ...).

calc_method.description: Calculation method used to derive the indicator value for this rule version. Prose summary of the catalogue entry's `measurement.formula`; carried inline for the same reason `definition` is.

value.description: Indicator value at `captured_at`. Numeric for ratio/count/duration units; SKELETON does not constrain shape beyond the JSON Schema `number` type. CORE-FANOUT keys the constraint off `unit`.

source_data.description: Pointer to the OCSF source-data shape the indicator was derived from. The framework references OCSF classes by `class_uid`; it does not maintain an OCSF fork.

ocsf_class_uid.description: OCSF class_uid the source data conforms to (e.g. 2001 for Security Finding, 4002 for Authentication Activity). Integer per the OCSF schema.

ocsf_class_name.description: Optional human-readable OCSF class name carried alongside the uid for reviewer convenience. Not authoritative — the uid is.

telemetry_ref.description: Optional pointer back to a SecOps-NG telemetry artifact under `content/telemetry/` when one exists (`telemetry.ocsf.<name>@v<n>` shape).

ref_viz.description: Reference-visualisation hint for the indicator. Lets the downstream F-CP-06 effectiveness evidence stream and the auditor-bundle render a default chart shape without per-metric custom code. Operator-overridable.

kind.description: Visualisation kind. SKELETON enum is intentionally small — CORE-FANOUT extends it as the per-target emitters land.

x_axis.description: Field path to the x-axis dimension when applicable (e.g. `captured_at` for a time-series line chart).

y_axis.description: Field path to the y-axis measurement (e.g. `metric.value`).

notes.description: Operator-facing prose hint about how the indicator is best read — 'lower is better', 'breach threshold at 0.25', etc.
